chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى حَمَّادٌ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ ذَبَحَ طَيْرًا فَقَطَعَ رَأْسَهُ أَ يُؤْكَلُ مِنْهُ

translations.en: That he was asked about a man who slaughtered a bird and severed its head: may it be eaten?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ «نَعَمْ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يَتَعَمَّدْ قَطْعَ رَأْسِهِ».

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "Yes, but he should not deliberately cut off its head."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a bird remains permissible to eat even if its head was severed during slaughter. At the same time, it teaches that one should not deliberately do so, indicating a disliked or improper manner in slaughter despite the meat remaining halal.
en.seo_question: Is a bird halal to eat if its head is cut off during slaughter?

key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ: it may be eaten; it is lawful to consume
key_terms.لَا يَتَعَمَّدْ: he should not do so intentionally or deliberately
